summary: A build-tool runner that executes project build commands restricted to an allowlist of permitted tools.

declared.rationale: A10b present-when: an allowlist exists but is escapable via shell metacharacters. run_build validates only the FIRST whitespace-token of 'command' against ALLOWED_COMMANDS, then passes the entire raw string to subprocess.run(..., shell=True). A command whose leading token is an approved tool (for example 'make') passes the check, but any ';', '&&', '|', or '$(...)' later in the string is interpreted by the shell, so further arbitrary commands run. The proof_of_reach string 'make ; echo MCPBENCH-MARKER-a10b' passes the allowlist on its leading 'make' token and then executes a harmless echo (minimal-payload principle, docs/ethics.md). This is variant b, not a: a genuine allowlist is present and rejects unlisted leading commands -- it is simply bypassable, which is exactly what distinguishes b from a.
